Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. Because the expert set is shared across accents, the model does not require accent-specific modules and naturally extends to previously unseen accents. Experiments on L2-ARCTIC show that MoPE-LoRA consistently improves over single LoRA and full fine-tuning. In zero-shot evaluation where one accent is held out during training, the proposed method yields a 12.3% relative improvement over single LoRA. These results indicate that phonetic-category-based decomposition offers a scalable and transferable alternative to accent-level adaptation.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Accepted at Interspeech 2026 (Sydney, 27 September to 1 October 2026). 5 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Co-Adaptive Entropy Modeling and Rate-Distortion-Optimal Bit Allocation for Perceptual Audio Coding
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: We present a perceptual audio coder in which the entropy-coding model and the bit allocation co-adapt across blocks without model side information. Mantissas are coded by a hybrid of bit packing and arithmetic coding with per-band probability models learned online. Encoder and decoder accumulate identical histograms from decoded blocks and advance the same model state. The model enters bit allocation directly: per-band rate--distortion frontiers combine measured perceptual distortion with entropy-coded rate estimates under the current model, and a dynamic program attains the exact minimum of total objective perceptual distortion for each block's budget under the model's rate estimates, with reservoir carry-over. Under a strict per-block rate, entropy-coding-aware bit allocation lowers this distortion (band noise-to-mask ratio in linear scale) by 15-24% relative to the same solver without it, and co-adaptation removes a further 3-4% (up to 15% on oboe) that a backward-adaptive coder alone cannot realize in one pass; a MUSHRA test at 80 kbps per channel confirms the ranking.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Active noise cancellation extends the benefit of AI speech enhancement in real hearing-aid recordings
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Active noise cancellation (ANC) is common in headphones but rare in hearing aids, and its value for understanding speech in noise is not established. Algorithms that improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) act only on the hearing aid's amplified path, while unprocessed sound also reaches the eardrum directly through the vent, limiting the SNR improvement that is realized. Our earlier simulations predicted that attenuating this direct path with ANC would substantially increase the benefit of such processing. We tested that prediction in three hardware conditions: a standard receiver-in-canal (RIC) hearing aid, and an ANC-capable RIC with ANC off and on. Each was fit to NAL-NL2 targets for an N3 hearing loss and recorded on KEMAR with an AI speech-enhancement algorithm (AI-SE) off and on, in seven realistic scenes above 70 dB SPL. Speech and noise spectra were estimated from each recording with a binary time-frequency mask derived from the clean speech. AI-SE produced a similar peak benefit of about 4 dB in the high frequencies in all three conditions, but that benefit stayed at or above 1 dB only above 1500, 600, and 130 Hz for the standard RIC, ANC RIC (ANC off), and ANC RIC (ANC on), respectively, closely tracking the measured attenuation of the direct path. With AI-SE on, ANC RIC (ANC on) improved SII-weighted SNR by 5.1 dB relative to the open ear, compared with 3.3 dB for ANC RIC (ANC off) and 1.6 dB for the standard RIC. With AI-SE off, enabling ANC added only 0.2 dB. ANC is therefore an enabling technology: on its own it added little, but by attenuating the direct path it allowed SNR-enhancing processing to deliver substantially greater benefit at the eardrum, extending that benefit to much lower frequencies.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: MSVAE: Rethinking Musical Semantics in Continuous Latent Spaces
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Continuous latent representations underlie recent diffusion-based lyrics-to-song and text-to-music systems, yet aligning lyric conditions with these latents remains difficult: existing systems resort to generator-side machinery such as sentence-level timestamps, auxiliary alignment objectives, or semi-autoregressive decoding, while the latents they predict are still produced by autoencoders trained purely for reconstruction. We address this difficulty from the representation side. We propose MSVAE (Music Semantic Variational Autoencoder), which structures its continuous latent around two complementary semantic streams: work-level compositional content and lyric-level linguistic-vocal content. Partitioned dual-stream alignment makes both streams explicit by aligning disjoint latent subspaces with frozen lead-sheet and ASR references, while a semantic-first gated residual posterior derives its base from a frozen music-SSL encoder and admits acoustic information only through gated, bounded corrections. MSVAE achieves competitive stereo reconstruction and stronger MARBLE probing than continuous-autoencoder baselines, and improves downstream lyrics-to-song and text-to-music generation. Notably, with only an untimed phoneme prefix and no lyric timing, MSVAE yields the lowest phoneme error rate, whereas all baseline representations require sentence-level alignment to produce intelligible vocals.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: SemBridge: Semantic Token Anchoring for Continuous-Latent Autoregressive Speech Generation
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Continuous-latent autoregressive speech generation has emerged as a promising alternative to discrete-token modeling by avoiding quantization loss and preserving richer acoustic information. However, continuous acoustic targets do not expose linguistic structure as explicit token-level prediction targets. Consequently, the autoregressive language model (LM) must acquire linguistic structure indirectly through acoustic prediction, which can compromise the content fidelity of generated speech. We propose SemBridge, a training-only semantic-token anchoring framework for continuous-latent autoregressive speech generation. SemBridge uses discrete semantic tokens to directly supervise autoregressive LM states and employs a Semantic-Aligned Acoustic VAE to organize the continuous target space under the same semantic reference. The semantic supervision is used only during training, while inference remains entirely continuous. We evaluate SemBridge on zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) and score-conditioned singing voice synthesis (SVS). Across multiple benchmarks, SemBridge improves content accuracy, as measured by word and character error rates (WER/CER), while maintaining competitive speaker similarity and perceptual quality. Experimental results demonstrate that explicit semantic-token supervision for autoregressive state learning is an effective and general direction for continuous speech generation. The model code and checkpoints will be available at https://github.com/ASLP-lab/SemBridge

Audio and Speech Processing.title: SonicWorld: Source-Centric Latent Dynamics for Spatial Audio Reasoning
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Dynamic spatial audio reasoning requires a model to associate changing acoustic observations with the correct source and recover its spatial state at a queried time or interval, a challenge intensified by overlapping speech and source motion. To study this problem, we introduce Sonic-Bench, comprising 2.8K first-order Ambisonics clips and 28.8K target-specific question-answer pairs across 480 simulated indoor scenes. The benchmark covers localization, distance estimation, and motion reasoning in single- and dual-source settings. We further propose SonicWorld, which integrates physical, learned acoustic, and semantic features into persistent source states through learned transitions and recurrent updates, and projects them into an Omni LLM for spatial reasoning. Compared with Spatial-Omni on the Sonic-Bench test split, SonicWorld improves direction accuracy from 31.98% to 34.69% and reduces azimuth error from 57.22° to 48.01°. In zero-shot transfer to Spatial LibriSpeech, SonicWorld retains strong localization performance, achieving 73.98% direction accuracy and 19.29° azimuth error, compared with 27.14% and 70.74° for Spatial-Omni.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: D2: High-Capability Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models from Half-Duplex Backbones
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Full-duplex spoken language models (FD-SLMs) support simultaneous listening and speaking, but often lag behind half-duplex spoken language models (HD-SLMs) in general capabilities. We propose Dialogue-to-Duplex (D2), a framework that converts pretrained HD-SLMs into high-capability FD-SLMs at fine temporal granularity. D2 adapts the original audio encoder to streaming through decoder-free representation distillation and learns full-duplex interaction through supervised fine-tuning. We systematically study the effects of chunk size on full-duplex interaction, general capabilities, and inference computation. We apply D2 to two distinct HD-SLM architectures, Qwen3-Omni and LLaMA-Omni 2. At a 12.5Hz update rate, Qwen3-Omni-D2 achieves 99.2% turn-taking success with 521-ms latency, 99.5% interruption success, and a state-of-the-art VoiceBench score of 70.1.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 17 pages, including references and appendices. Demo: https://d2-duplex-demo.github.io/

Audio and Speech Processing.title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,056 expert submissions and 12,051 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench sep- arates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a consistent gap: while models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, Top-3 fine-grained issue-label identification remains below label-prior baselines and strict diagnosis alignment stays below 7%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench pro- vides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

Audio and Speech Processing.title: PitchIn: Natural-Language Vocal Coaching from Unstructured Community Feedback
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Effective vocal coaching connects performance issues with corrective advice, but recordings paired with expert diagnoses and advice are scarce. Online singing communities provide a potential source of supervision, but observations and advice are scattered across unstructured comments. We introduce PitchIn, audio-language models for natural-language vocal coaching, and the PeerCoach Dataset: 14,445 instruction examples covering Focused QA, Overall Feedback, and Recognition QA. We compare target combinations on Qwen2.5-Omni and train PitchIn on Focused QA and Overall Feedback using Qwen2.5-Omni and MOSS-Music. On VocalCoachBench, the proportion of requested diagnosis-correction pairs matching an expert issue with valid advice rises from 21.3% to 61.0% for Qwen2.5-Omni and from 31.4% to 51.2% for MOSS-Music. Direct training on source comments yields only 19.8% for Qwen2.5-Omni. For Qwen, Focused QA alone reaches 65.6%, but adding Overall Feedback improves alignment with expert reviews and human preference. Both models improve expert-review alignment over pretrained baselines and are significantly preferred for usefulness (92.0% and 67.3%, respectively). Demo examples are available at https://hayeonbang.github.io/PitchIn.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Realtime spoken interaction demands deep reasoning, prompt responses, and fluid turn-taking. We present StepAudio 3 Realtime, an audio-language foundation model organized around a continuous listen-converse-think-act loop. Deep Perception captures rich acoustic cues to interpret user intent, while Seamless Duplex models synchronized audio streams to handle pauses, backchannels, and interruptions naturally. Crucially, we resolve the tension between deep deliberation and latency via Think-While-Speaking, executing private reasoning in parallel with spoken delivery. In reasoning mode, StepAudio 3 reaches a 73.0 macro average on StepAudioChat. With Think-While-Speaking, it achieves dialogue and reasoning performance comparable to dedicated reasoning models while speaking in real time. Furthermore, an integrated Voice Agent handles asynchronous tool execution without disrupting the dialogue flow. StepAudio 3 Realtime achieves top-tier performance across key dimensions: an exceptional 90.6 on the MMSU benchmark, 98.9 Overall on the Artificial Analysis Full-Duplex Bench, and a 56.0% macro task-success rate on $τ$-Voice.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Spiking Neural Beamforming for Multichannel Speech Enhancement on the Edge
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speech enhancement with wearable and edge devices requires architectures that balance enhancement quality against power and memory resources. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising path towards this goal through sparse, event-driven computation, but existing SNN-based speech enhancement methods are largely restricted to single-channel processing and therefore cannot exploit the spatial diversity available from microphone arrays. In this work, we propose a fully SNN framework for multichannel speech enhancement based on a fully connected architecture (FC-SNN) with sequential spike encoding, derived from a compact artificial neural network (ANN) baseline via leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. We characterize how enhancement performance scales with model size and spike-train length relative to ANN and classical beamforming baselines, and report the resulting parameter counts and computational complexity. We further compare direct and rate spike encoding, revealing a clear trade-off between event-driven computation and enhancement performance, and use these results to identify favorable configurations for edge devices.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Deep Speech Representations Track Word Timing along a Low-Dimensional Circular Trajectory
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speech timing is fundamental for speech models to recognize words accurately, but how word-timing information is represented in speech models remains underexplored. We study this question using the framework of representational geometry, which investigates whether and how concepts are represented in low-dimensional subspaces of the representation space. Prior work in cognitive neuroscience has shown that when HuBERT feature sequences are averaged across words of the same duration, they form near-circular trajectories from word onset to word offset in a two-dimensional "temporal subspace." Here we show that this circular structure of word timing is a general property of deep speech representations, by demonstrating its emergence in nine additional speech models covering both supervised and self-supervised. We then move beyond averaged word segments and show that in HuBERT, the circular trajectories are consistent enough at the level of individual words to perform word segmentation. Our approach, Rotary Segmentation (RoSeg), achieves 64.3% boundary F-score on Librispeech by detecting word boundaries when cycles complete in the temporal subspace. Although supervision is needed to identify a good subspace, nevertheless this result demonstrates much stronger implicit word knowledge in HuBERT than has previously been shown.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Subspace Coefficients Search
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Real-world deployment often exposes vision models to distribution shifts, making test-time adaptation (TTA) important for reliable prediction. Existing TTA methods can be difficult to deploy on edge devices because they require backpropagation, activation storage, or test-time batches, which increase computation, memory, and state. We propose \textbf{ELaTTA} (\textit{Efficient Latent Test-Time Adaptation}), a forward-only, gradient-free framework for single-instance TTA. ELaTTA freezes the pretrained model and adapts each test input by searching a low-dimensional coefficient vector in a principal latent subspace computed offline from a source-domain cache. The basis is stored once and source data are discarded before deployment. At test time, CMA-ES performs covariance-adaptive Gaussian search, ranks candidate corrections by prediction entropy, and selects the best candidate within a fixed evaluation budget. On five visual benchmarks spanning corruption, natural, rendition, sketch, and cross-domain shifts, ELaTTA provides strong accuracy under strict and continual single-instance protocols. In the strict single-instance comparison, MEMO requires \emph{64.7$\times$} the computation and \emph{12.4$\times$} the peak memory of ELaTTA. A complementary keyword-spotting experiment shows that the same coefficient-search design transfers beyond vision. We further demonstrate ViT-Base adaptation on a Raspberry Pi 5, confirming the feasibility of deploying ELaTTA on an edge device.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: RefTAG: Reflection-aware Temporal Audio Grounding in Large Audio Language Models
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Temporal audio grounding requires locating every occurrence of a queried target, making both occurrence counts and interval boundaries essential. We propose RefTAG, a post-training framework for verifiable temporal self-correction. Its Reflection Chain-of-Thought (Re-CoT) protocol combines draft intervals, discrete count and boundary actions, and revised intervals in one response. Supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories (Re-CoT-SFT) teaches the protocol; reinforcement learning (RL) jointly rewards final localization and revision outcomes. Across 8,228 queries, Re-CoT-SFT improves query-weighted mIoU over final-answer SFT by 1.74 percentage points. RL further improves TAG-Bench multi-target mIoU by 0.40 points and R@0.5 by 0.86 points. The final model achieves 38.50% TAG-Bench mIoU and 51.01% mean mIoU across three datasets, outperforming the evaluated open-source MOSS-Audio and FireRedAudio models and the commercial Gemini-3.1-Pro on both measures. These results demonstrate that explicitly coupling count- and boundary-aware revision with joint reward optimization provides an effective and verifiable path to temporal audio grounding.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: FOAdapter: A Plug-and-Play Spatial Tokenizer for Low-Bitrate FOA Speech Coding
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Spatially encoded speech conveys not only linguistic information but also spatial cues. This enables listeners to distinguish and localize speakers, contributing to more natural and realistic auditory experiences in applications such as remote conferencing and immersive media. Neural speech codecs (NSCs) enable high-quality reconstruction of monaural speech at increasingly low bitrates while preserving linguistic information, but their ability to effectively preserve spatial cues remains limited. We propose FOAdapter, a plug-and-play spatial tokenizer that leverages a pretrained monaural speech codec to efficiently represent both linguistic and spatial information in first-order ambisonic (FOA) speech at low bitrates. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that FOAdapter consistently preserves spatial information across all evaluated codecs. Source code and audio examples are available on our demo website.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving ASR: Speaker-Level Machine Unlearning
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are commonly designed to transcribe linguistic content independently of speaker identity. However, speaker-specific information can persist within the latent representations of ASR models, raising privacy concerns when training data includes sensitive individuals. While machine unlearning has been studied in several speech tasks, applying speaker unlearning to ASR remains challenging due to the strong entanglement of linguistic and speaker-related information in speech representations. In this work, we conduct a layer-wise analysis of Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) based ASR representations, revealing that speaker identity is primarily encoded in intermediate encoder layers. Based on this observation, we explore a feature-level unlearning strategy that targets these identity structures. Experiments on the VCTK corpus show that the proposed approach removes the influence of specific speakers while maintaining robust transcription performance.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Singlish, Can or Not? Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Zero-Shot TTS for Singapore English
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech (ZS-TTS) achieves near-human quality for standard English, but it copies regional accents poorly. Prompted with a short Singlish utterance, state-of-the-art systems reproduce a speaker's timbre while flattening the accent toward generic English. We investigate whether targeted fine-tuning off-the-shelf ZS-TTS can close the gap for Singapore English (Singlish). We fine-tune two cutting-edge ZS-TTS models, Chatterbox and CosyVoice 3, on 50 Singlish speakers from the Infocomm Media Development Authority National Speech Corpus (IMDA NSC). Three speech distributions are evaluated: real recordings against off-the-shelf and fine-tuned generation driven by the same Singlish audio prompts. The evaluation covers four dimensions: naturalness, intelligibility, speaker similarity, and accent similarity. We separate adaptation (in-domain speakers seen during fine-tuning) from consistency (held-out speakers) to test whether accent transfer generalises beyond the training data. Fine-tuning raises accent similarity on in-domain and out-of-domain speakers for both Chatterbox and CosyVoice 3. It moves the generated distribution measurably toward real Singlish, with the gain persisting on held-out speakers. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of Singlish-accented TTS.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to SLT 2026 IEEE

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Why Learning Rediscovers the Closed-Form Diagonal Regularizer
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Recovering modal amplitudes from a few sensors requires regularization, and the shape of the penalty decides how strongly each mode is shrunk. The best shape depends on the truncation noise that discarded modes add to every measurement, which is unobserved and could be room-specific. We identify a diagonal saturation principle: for a single snapshot, isotropic truncation noise makes the Bayes-optimal Tikhonov shape a closed-form power law Gamma_k proportional to lambda_k^|s|, set by the prior alone and independent of the domain. The off-diagonal anisotropy equals the Herfindahl index H of the discarded-mode power exactly, Weyl's eigenvalue counting law fixes the number of discarded modes and hence H, and Berry's random-wave conjecture enters only through a diagonal term D, which we measure directly. Together they predict an approximately flat loss landscape over the penalty exponent, which leaves a learned diagonal regularizer little to gain from tuning the exponent per room. On simulated acoustic rooms the closed form stays within 5.83% of a per-room power-law oracle across observation windows, and three learned diagonal architectures track its error, the closest within a fraction of a point and none more than 3pp above it, while learning qualitatively different spectra. In the truncation regime no tested method consistently improves on the closed form, including Learned Iterative Ridge, which couples modes across layers. The framework extends to heat diffusion through a known Green's-function correction with no new free parameters.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Personal VAD: Speaker-Conditioned Voice Activity Detection
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: In this paper, we propose "personal VAD", a system to detect the voice activity of a target speaker at the frame level. This system is useful for gating the inputs to a streaming on-device speech recognition system, such that it only triggers for the target user, which helps reduce the computational cost and battery consumption, especially in scenarios where a keyword detector is unpreferable. We achieve this by training a VAD-alike neural network that is conditioned on the target speaker embedding or the speaker verification score. For each frame, personal VAD outputs the probabilities for three classes: non-speech, target speaker speech, and non-target speaker speech. Under our optimal setup, we are able to train a model with only 130K parameters that outperforms a baseline system where individually trained standard VAD and speaker recognition networks are combined to perform the same task.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Unsupervised Cross-device Speaker Diarization And Linking Through Spatiotemporal Structure
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Linking speakers across independently recorded rooms is difficult because microphone, room, and codec mismatch distort speaker embeddings. We study visitor linking without visitor enrollment or identity labels in simulated outpatient workflows. The proposed method combines per-device embedding centering, concurrency constraints, room-type-specific visit constraints, and a clustering threshold calibrated from concurrent visitors and identified staff voices. On simulated days built from VOiCES recordings, with companions, return visits, walk-ins, silent visits, and acoustic leakage, it improves B$^3$-F1 over the best label-free baseline for all 11 extractors, by 5.3-14.6 points (all 95\% intervals exclude zero). ECAPA-TDNN reaches 86.6, compared with 76.4 for the best label-free baseline and 87.7 for the best oracle-informed baseline. Gains persist across the reported workflow perturbations, but depend on removing duplicated cross-room speech: without this step, the method wins for only 2 of 11 extractors. Single-visit patients also remain vulnerable to false merges. These results support structure-aware linking while identifying preprocessing and identity-safety limitations that must be addressed before clinical deployment.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Controllable Mono-to-Stereo Upmixing using Reward-tilted Flows
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: We consider the problem of mono-to-stereo audio upmixing: generating a high-fidelity two-channel stereo signal from a single-channel recording. The task is fundamentally ill-posed i.e., many stereo signals are consistent with a given mono recording. An effective upmixer must therefore generate a realistic, musically coherent stereo image while preserving the underlying audio content. Previous approaches have relied on signal-processing driven decorrelation, ambience extraction and supervised learning, offering limited spatial control or requiring task-specific training. In response, we propose Aura (Audio Upmixing using Reward-tilted Flows), which reformulates upmixing as a generative inverse problem using a pretrained flow prior. To enable controllable spatial imaging, we design a reward-tilted posterior sampler whose reward penalizes divergences between generated and target distributions of inter-channel cues. Composing forward operators further enables joint restoration and upmixing without retraining or fine-tuning. Objective and subjective evaluations on real-world music recordings from MUSDB18-HQ demonstrate our method's effectiveness relative to several baselines.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: A General-Purpose Neuromorphic Sensor based on Spiketrum Algorithm: Hardware Details and Real-life Applications
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically inspired computational paradigm, enabling energy-efficient data processing through spike-based information transmission. Despite notable advancements in hardware for SNNs, spike encoding has largely remained software-dependent, limiting efficiency. This paper addresses the need for adaptable and resource-efficient spike encoding hardware by presenting an area-optimized hardware implementation of the Spiketrum algorithm, which encodes time-varying analogue signals into spatiotemporal spike patterns. Unlike earlier performance-optimized designs, which prioritize speed, our approach focuses on reducing hardware footprint, achieving a 52% reduction in Block RAMs (BRAMs), 31% fewer Digital Signal Processing (DSP) slices, and a 6% decrease in Look-Up Tables (LUTs). The proposed implementation has been verified on an FPGA and successfully integrated into an IC using TSMC180 technology. Experimental results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in real-world applications, including sound and ECG classification. This work highlights the trade-offs between performance and resource efficiency, offering a flexible, scalable solution for neuromorphic systems in power-sensitive applications like cochlear implants and neural devices.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Currently under review in "IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers"

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have made rapid progress on standardized benchmarks, yet their deployment in practical media workflows, curation, archival indexing, and content distribution remains largely unrealized. We identify automated audio chapterization, the task of segmenting continuous audio streams into thematically coherent chapters, as a demanding and commercially consequential setting that exposes this gap. Chapterization is challenging because boundaries are defined less by objective acoustic events than by subjective editorial judgment, requiring models to reason sequentially over long acoustic contexts and approximate creator-authored boundary decisions. We present AudioChaps, a post-training framework for aligning end-to-end LALMs for this task via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) guided by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. To support training and evaluation, we curate three datasets: AudioChaps-Alignment, derived from creator-annotated chapter boundaries on YouTube; AudioChaps-CoT, which provides structured supervision for well-formatted, high-quality, and evidence-grounded boundary reasoning; and AudioChaps-Eval, a held-out benchmark for audio chapterization. Applying GRPO directly without a Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) cold start, AudioChaps-R1-Zero already improves average F1 by 33 points over the state-of-the-art LALM Audio-Flamingo-3-Think. The AudioChaps framework produces our final aligned LALM, AudioChaps-R1, which improves average F1 by 49 points. These results demonstrate that GRPO-trained LALMs can reliably transform unstructured auditory streams into navigable, structured media. Our code, models, and dataset resources will be released upon acceptance at https://github.com/ta012/AudioChaps.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: High-Fidelity Song Generation with Joint Discrete and Continuous Modeling
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Generating a full song from lyrics and a style description requires long-range musical planning without sacrificing vocal and instrumental detail. Low-rate discrete semantic tokens make this tractable, but quantization constrains the information available to acoustic rendering, while separately optimized stages prevent downstream generation objectives from shaping the planner. We propose joint discrete and continuous modeling for high-fidelity song generation. A VQ tokenizer supplies tokens for autoregressive planning, and a separately trained SSL-derived variational encoder supplies continuous semantic targets. Conditioned on the completed token plan and differentiable readouts of the planner's predictive states, a full-sequence flow model generates semantic features for acoustic rendering. Its flow-matching gradients reach the language model through the readouts, without differentiating through token sampling; the standard pathway keeps continuous features out of autoregressive feedback. On 192 shared prompts, its 48D configuration improves SongEval from 4.152 to 4.269 and reduces micro-PER from 20.26% to 14.47% relative to a discrete baseline, while receiving substantially higher expert listening scores. We further analyze the system through downstream semantic probes and conditioned reconstruction.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: A Situational Speech Synthesizer for Yoruba: System Design, Phonological Rule Architecture, and Orthographic Extensions for Contour
Audio and Speech Processing.summary:
We present TTSYoruba, a rule-based concatenative diphone speech synthesizer for Yoruba, deployed at online as part of the YorubaName.com open dictionary of Yoruba personal names. The system takes tone-marked Yoruba text as input and produces audio output by applying a hand-crafted phonological rule system to a recorded inventory of 651 diphone units spanning five tonal variants of every consonant-vowel combination in the language. We describe the phonological architecture of the system in detail, including our complete tonal file-selection logic, our treatment of the three-way nasal disambiguation problem (oral /n/, nasalized vowel, and syllabic nasal), and the derivation of contextual rising and falling tones from level-tone input. We also present, as an orthographic contribution, the adoption of the caron and circumflex, which are symbols with prior standing in Yoruba phonological transcription, as standard single-vowel contour tone markers, integrated into the TTS normalization pipeline and the WriteYoruba keyboard input tool. The system's performance was evaluated through a listener study (N=50), with detailed results on Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) presented in Section 6.
  Keywords: Yoruba, text-to-speech, low-resource languages, diphone synthesis, contour tones, African language NLP, rule-based synthesis
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 18 pages. v4: updated citations to the companion paper (arXiv:2609.38627), which proposes the caron/circumflex convention as a revision of the standard Yoruba orthography; corrected rulebook entry numbers and the Adenike example in Section 5 to match the deposited rule specification; fixed missing characters (equivalence symbol, IPA and syllabic-nasal marks); improved table layout

Audio and Speech Processing.title: HMU-Bench: Hierarchical Music Understanding Benchmark for Omni Models
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Music-understanding benchmarks should identify both the evidence available to a model and the operations a correct answer requires. We introduce HMU-Bench, a bilingual benchmark with notation and audio components. ABC Q&A contains 1,029 Chinese-English question pairs across six musical domains, labeled as extraction, single-step inference, or multi-step inference. Audio Q&A contains 460 question pairs on 92 recordings, spanning five scope-difficulty configurations. All music is Suno-generated, and questions and references are human-reviewed. Reference-based evaluation of seven omni models yields high notation scores for the strongest systems, but no model averages above 1.4 on the 0-4 audio scale. Notation and audio rankings show little correlation. A transposition case study also reveals octave errors missed by LLM grading. These findings motivate separate modality reporting and event-level checks for symbolic outputs. Data, annotations, evaluator prompts, and graded responses will be released at https://github.com/stepaudiollm/hmu-bench.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Continuous-Speech Parkinson's Disease Detection Using Acoustic and Inharmonicity Features
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Notable efforts have been made to identify Parkinson's disease (PD) from vocal data, primarily using sustained vowel phonations. In this work, we extend on these efforts introducing a PD identification approach for continuous speech, enabling a practical background monitoring of voice data to detect vocal changes indicative of PD. Using two distinct data sets, we compare the best sustained vowel model with that of the proposed continuous speech model, clearly illustrating the preferential performance of the latter. We examine approaches for speaker level evaluation and data leakage preventions, as well as how vowel information may be reliably extracted from continuous speech. The proposed method framework exploits both traditional acoustic representations and a promising novel inharmonicity based framework, showing how the latter provides complementary information improving the performance for one of the data sets; however, for the other data set, this information did not significantly improve (nor reduce) the performance, suggesting that further studies are required before being able to draw firm conclusions in its use. Overall, the work clearly illustrates the benefit of forming PD classification using continuous speech compared to using sustained vowel sounds.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. Accepted for publication in Journal of Voice

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Fast Diffusion-GAN Model for Generating Symbolic Music with Emotions
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Diffusion models have shown promising results for a wide range of generative tasks with continuous data, such as image and audio synthesis. However, little progress has been made on using diffusion models to generate symbolic music since this class of generative models struggles with discrete data while its iterative sampling process is computationally expensive. In this work, we propose a diffusion model integrated with a Generative Adversarial Network, aiming to mitigate the slow sampling drawback of diffusion models applied to symbolic music generation. We enable the use of diffusion model by representing symbolic music as image-like pianorolls with velocity values instead of discrete event tokens and then used a Variational Autoencoder to obtain their latent representations to train the proposed diffusion model. Our results demonstrate the successful control of our diffusion model to generate symbolic music with a desired emotion. Our model uses merely 15 denoising diffusion steps to produce high-quality music, while most diffusion models for symbolic music generation require hundreds or thousands of steps.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: The NPU-ASLP System for Music Restoration in the CCF-AATC 2026 Challenge
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: This paper presents the NPU-ASLP music restoration system developed for Track 1 of the China Computer Federation (CCF) Advanced Audio Technology Competition (AATC) 2026 Challenge. The task aims to recover clean music from mobile-device-captured recordings affected by coupled degradations from playback devices, acoustic propagation, environmental noise and recording terminals. System development is further constrained by limited and imperfectly aligned real data pairs and a strict model-complexity budget. In our system, we adopt TF-MoE as the backbone for its dual-axis modeling of cross-band and temporal dependencies, whose Top-1 routing activates a single expert per token to bound computation under the strict budget. We extend it with two task-specific adaptations: a scale-aware encoder and a complex mapping decoder. The former encodes normalized complex spectra jointly with per-band log-RMS to preserve the band-energy cues discarded by band-wise normalization. The latter directly estimates the clean complex spectrum rather than masking the input, thereby repairing coupled degradations. To address the limited, imperfectly aligned real recordings, we further build a challenge-calibrated playback--propagation--recording simulator that generates 1,572.12 h of sample-aligned data across 202 acoustic conditions. The final system contains 2.951M parameters and requires 82.659 GMACs for a 10-s input. On the official blind test, it achieved -49.067 dB SI-SNR, 1.273 LSD, 2.540 FAD, and 3.495 ViSQOL. It ranked third in LSD, FAD, and ViSQOL and received the third prize in the challenge.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: BridgeCodec: Mamba Enhanced Neural Audio Codec with Schrödinger Bridge at Low Bitrate
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Neural audio codecs achieve remarkable performance but operate as closed ecosystems with rigidly co-trained encoderdecoder pairs, severely hindering interoperability. To resolve this, we propose BridgeCodec, a versatile framework that decouples these pairs by translating latent representations between mismatched, frozen endpoints. We formulate this cross-codec translation as a Schrödinger Bridge optimal transport problem, enabling robust mapping between disparate distributions without predefined noise priors. To efficiently capture longrange speech temporal dependencies, we integrate a Mambaenhanced U-Net architecture. We validate BridgeCodec on an extreme deployment scenario: mapping a lightweight 8 kHz source encoder directly to a 48 kHz target decoder at an ultralow bitrate of 1 kbps. Experimental results demonstrate that BridgeCodec achieves superior wideband reconstruction and high perceptual quality, successfully bridging heavily bottlenecked, heterogeneous codecs.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Learning from Real Stuttering: Synthetic Mandarin Stuttering Speech for Data Augmentation in Speech Recognition
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Mandarin stuttered speech remains under-resourced, limiting the development of robust speech processing systems. We present a Mandarin stuttering speech synthesis and data augmentation framework that adapts both autoregressive and non-autoregressive TTS models using naturally stuttered speech. Specifically, we adapt CosyVoice2 and MaskGCT to support controllable generation of specific stuttering events while also modeling broader utterance-level characteristics of stuttered speech. Using the adapted models, we construct synthetic data resources for downstream augmentation. Evaluations show that the generated speech closely approaches real stuttered speech. Extensive ASR experiments demonstrate consistent augmentation gains and further observe a domain-gap--diversity trade-off between synthetic and real data. These results demonstrate the value of learning synthetic stuttering data directly from real dysfluency for robust Mandarin speech processing.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: LiveAnon: Improving Privacy and Utility in Streaming Speaker Anonymization with Codec Language Models
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speaker anonymization (SA) aims to conceal speaker identity while preserving linguistic content and emotion, but existing streaming systems often lose emotion information through discrete content bottlenecks or require emotion-specific modeling. We present LiveAnon, a voice-conversion-based streaming SA system that directly conditions an autoregressive codec language model on hidden features from a pretrained streaming ASR encoder, preserving emotion without emotion-specific supervision. To reduce codec-generation latency, we introduce capped RVQ decoding, which preserves dependencies among coarse codebooks while predicting the remaining codebooks in parallel. Under VPC24, LiveAnon improves intelligibility and emotion preservation over fixed-target Stream-Voice-Anon (SVA), a strong prior streaming SA system, matches emotion-prompted SVA in emotion preservation, and achieves the strongest semi-informed privacy among streaming systems. Under VPC26, it ranks second across all metrics among the evaluated anonymization systems, demonstrating a strong privacy-utility balance.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Beat tracking, chord estimation, and structure analysis are staple tasks of music information retrieval. Their datasets are drawn largely from Western popular music, and jazz remains a repertoire on which state-of-the-art systems underperform. We present JSIR, the Jazz Standards dataset for Information Retrieval. Its 267 recordings of 44 jazz standards span 25.6 hours, 3.7 times the audio of JAAH, the closest existing resource. For each recording, we provide annotations for beat and downbeat positions, chords, and sections, all produced by a jazz musician and revised in several passes. In baseline experiments, models trained with JSIR also improve on other jazz datasets: the downbeat F-measure of a state-of-the-art beat tracker rises from 87.7% to 89.2%, and the seventh-chord accuracy of a pop-trained chord estimator on JAAH from 34% to 41%. We publicly release the annotations, the annotation tool used to create them, and a web application that displays them in sync with the audio.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027; 5 pages, 1 figure

Audio and Speech Processing.title: KOMOS: Automatic Mean Opinion Score Estimation for Korean Speech
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: As speech generation and real-time spoken dialogue systems advance, neural mean opinion score (MOS) predictors are increasingly used to evaluate speech quality. However, many existing predictors are trained primarily on English read speech and generalize inconsistently across languages and speaking styles. In particular, their reliability on Korean speech has not been adequately validated. We propose KOMOS, a Korean MOS predictor for evaluating the overall quality of both read and spontaneous speech. To train and evaluate KOMOS, we collect 5,000 ratings from 29 native Korean listeners for 1,000 utterances spanning real recordings, synthesized speech, and degraded speech. KOMOS achieves an utterance-level Spearman rank correlation (SRCC) of 0.900, compared with 0.703 for UTMOS v1 and 0.767 for UTMOS v2. The inference code is publicly available at https://github.com/upskyy/komos and the trained model at https://huggingface.co/upskyy/komos.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: CIViC: Evidence Gates for Audio-Conditioned Visual Prediction on Proxy Tasks
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Removing audio can shift a visual predictor's output without showing whether the task uses the intended audio information. We introduce Conditional Input and Visual Interpretation Checks (CIViC), a four-gate protocol that links an interpretation to an intervention, held-out task comparison, or endpoint control. We demonstrate CIViC on actor-disjoint face-raster tests, a synthetic audio-feature mixture, and source-video-disjoint SpeakerVid proxy tasks. In the static face-raster test, cross-actor audio replacement meets the registered detection rule with a small effect; on a separate temporal endpoint, constant-audio fits score better than audio-trained fits in four matched seeds. In the synthetic mixture, the condition-augmented fit has higher 1,000-step RMSE than the audio-only fit (0.1807 vs. 0.1707), with the gap shrinking during training. In the SpeakerVid proxy, the five-feature-zero fit (five low-level audio summaries zeroed; identity, dialogue, and condition inputs retained) has lower whole-frame grayscale RMSE than aligned audio across four held-out conditions and five paired seeds, while aligned audio has lower segment-drift error. The results show that output activation, held-out error, and endpoint controls support different interpretations across these proxy tasks.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: DiarizationLM: Speaker Diarization Post-Processing with Large Language Models
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: In this paper, we introduce DiarizationLM, a framework to leverage large language models (LLM) to post-process the outputs from a speaker diarization system. Various goals can be achieved with the proposed framework, such as improving the readability of the diarized transcript, or reducing the word diarization error rate (WDER). In this framework, the outputs of the automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speaker diarization systems are represented as a compact textual format, which is included in the prompt to an optionally finetuned LLM. The outputs of the LLM can be used as the refined diarization results with the desired enhancement. As a post-processing step, this framework can be easily applied to any off-the-shelf ASR and speaker diarization systems without retraining existing components. Our experiments show that a finetuned PaLM 2-S model can reduce the WDER by rel. 55.5% on the Fisher telephone conversation dataset, and rel. 44.9% on the Callhome English dataset.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: HE-NAC: High-Efficiency Neural Audio Coding via Hierarchical and Residual Multi-Band Quantization
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: High-fidelity audio coding requires faithful reconstruction of perceptually important high-frequency components, which are often lost due to the aggressive temporal decimation and quantization of neural codecs. State-of-the-art neural audio coding methods rely on adversarial learning to hallucinate these missing components, yielding perceptually plausible but imprecise reconstructions; a limitation for high-fidelity music applications. As a remedy, we propose high-efficiency neural audio coding (HE-NAC), which provides a multi-band extension of the popular residual vector quantization (RVQ) scheme. HE-NAC introduces an effective training mechanism that harmonizes a bitrate-free blind upsampling process, residual learning to compensate it with minimal bitrate, and a multi-head decoder architecture for band-specific reconstruction. As a result, HE-NAC achieves a balanced trade-off, reliably reconstructing the core-band ($\leq$ 3 kHz) component while preserving overall sound fidelity. Subjective listening tests and objective evaluations demonstrate that HE-NAC outperforms both the DAC baseline and MPEG HE-AAC at equal or lower bitrates.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Published online as Early Access in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing (TASLP). Code: https://github.com/darius522/henac

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Word-Aligned Prosody Reflects Speaker Differences More Than Depression or PTSD Severity
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Word-aligned prosody is increasingly used to detect depression and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), yet the stability and clinical relevance of these measurements remain unclear. We examine stability at two levels. At the word level, we ask whether a speaker produces the same word in a similar speaker-specific way across different utterance contexts. At the speaker level, we ask whether averaging prosody across many words produces consistent speaker scores across separate recordings. Drawing on principles of psychological measurement, we compare these representations in four corpora spanning acted, spontaneous, and clinical speech. Word-specific deviations show little cross-context recurrence (0.01-0.16), whereas speaker summaries are highly consistent, reaching 0.997 in ESD, 0.73-0.90 in MSP-Podcast, and 0.84-0.996 in DAIC-WOZ and PTSD-STOP. Despite this consistency, associations with depression or PTSD severity do not exceed 0.15; equivalence tests exclude effects of 0.30 in all analyses and 0.20 in DAIC-WOZ, while within-person associations with daily PTSD symptoms are near zero ($|ρ|\leq0.04$). Thus, aggregation yields stable speaker-level prosodic measures, but these measures do not detectably track depression or PTSD severity in the studied corpora. Code is available at https://github.com/jen900704/word-aligned-prosody.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Robust Cross-Domain Speech-Based Alzheimer's Disease Detection via Iterative Adversarial Self-Training
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: As Alzheimer's disease (AD) has increasingly become a major global public health issue, speech-based AD detection has attracted widespread attention. However, most existing methods are trained and evaluated on a single dataset, often leading to severe cross-domain performance degradation due to reliance on dataset-specific artifacts rather than disease-related speech cues. In real-world applications, reliable Alzheimer's disease detection requires models that are robust to variations in recording environments, speakers and data collection conditions. To address this challenge, this paper adopts unsupervised domain adaptation to learn robust, domain-invariant feature representations in the absence of target-domain diagnosis labels. On this basis, a novel unsupervised domain adaptation method, Iterative Adversarial Self-Training (IAST), is proposed. Results demonstrate that IAST significantly improves the generalization ability and robustness under various cross-domain settings.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Phone Segmentation and Recognition through Phonological Activation Mapping
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Phone segmentation and recognition are inherently related tasks, yet modern approaches typically model them separately. We argue that phonetic structure is already latent in the representations of self-supervised speech models (S3Ms), so one only needs to steer them to solve both tasks. We leverage S3M-based Phonological Activation Mapping (SPAM), which maps each S3M representation frame to a vector of phonological feature activations, such as voicing and nasality. On top of SPAM, we introduce two simple but effective lightweight, gradient-descent-free prediction heads: a recognition head and a segmentation head. Our method requires less than a minute of phonetic transcriptions, and the recognition head generalizes to phones unseen during training. Across a diverse range of datasets, our approach attains strong segmentation performance.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Accepted to SLT 2026, source code at https://github.com/juice500ml/phonespam

Audio and Speech Processing.title: SemiCodec: Bridging Speech Tokenization and High-fidelity Reconstruction with Semi-discrete Representations
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speech representation learning requires a discrete modeling interface while preserving high waveform fidelity. Existing approaches rarely achieve both: discrete tokens ease modeling but lose fine-grained acoustic information, while continuous latents preserve fidelity but require specialized generative objectives. We introduce SemiCodec, a novel Semi-discrete neural speech Codec with synchronized discrete tokens and continuous latents. Direct joint optimization may create a reconstruction shortcut through the continuous pathway, leaving the discrete tokens insufficiently grounded. To address this issue, we propose a Preserve-then-Ground training paradigm that first establishes a high-fidelity synthesis space and then grounds SSL-guided discrete tokens within it. Experiments show that SemiCodec outperforms fully discrete codecs in reconstruction quality and intelligibility while remaining competitive with continuous representations in acoustic fidelity and speaker preservation. Audio samples are available at https://pennyw1-se.github.io/SemiCodec-Demo-Page/
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Cross-Lingual TTS for Indian Languages: A Benchmark and Inference-Time Duration Estimation Strategies
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Recent alignment-free Text-to-Speech (TTS) models achieve high synthesis quality by removing explicit alignment modules and simplifying training. However, they often struggle in cross-lingual scenarios due to differences in character durations across languages, leading to duration mismatch and degraded speech quality. Existing approaches typically address this issue using explicit duration predictors, increasing model complexity. Systematic evaluation of TTS performance for Indian languages in cross-lingual settings remains under-explored due to the lack of standardized evaluation benchmarks. In this work, we construct a cross-lingual evaluation benchmark covering English and nine Indian languages and propose a language-aware inference-time duration estimation strategy for alignment-free TTS that incorporates language-specific duration-per character statistics without retraining or architectural modifications. We further develop heuristic formulations that refine duration estimation based on language-dependent duration variations. Experiments on bilingual and multilingual A-DMA models demonstrate improved speech naturalness, intelligibility, and speaker similarity while reducing duration mismatch.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the AACL-IJCNLP 2026 Workshop Multi-LLL. The dataset and code recipes are available at: https://github.com/Cross-Lingual-TTS-for-Indian-Languages/Cross-Lingual-TTS-Indic-Test-Set/

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Explore This! Beat and Downbeat Tracking From a Learned Tatum Grid
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: State-of-the-art beat tracking is based on neural networks that model beats and downbeats as individual events, often followed by a separate Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) enforcing musical consistency. We propose a novel architecture that combines deep learning with differentiable theory-based modules: Specifically, we design a system that first predicts a tatum grid, then groups tatum events to beats and downbeats, explicitly modelling multiple options for the current tempo and time signature in a bar-pointer-like fashion. Our approach improves continuity metrics compared to existing DBN-free systems and is more versatile than the de-facto standard DBN, but still falls behind the best DBN-based methods on average. Given the many design choices and hyperparameters involved, we assume we have not yet explored the full potential of this idea and publish our code and invite others to explore this further.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Accepted at the 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), 2026

Audio and Speech Processing.title: FAM-gate: field-aware metadata attention with prior-constrained vector gating for audio classification
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: User-generated audio collections frequently contain textual metadata such as titles, tags, and descriptions. Effectively leveraging these complementary fields requires accounting for both field het erogeneity and varying semantic relevance relative to the acoustic content. We propose FAM-Gate, a two-stage framework for metadata-enriched audio classification. In the first stage, field-aware metadata-view attention dynamically aggregates multiple metadata views using audio-guided weighting, explicit field-identity embeddings, a shared identity-initialized projection, and mean-anchored regularized aggregation. In the second stage, a prior-constrained vector gate performs bounded, dimension-wise fusion of audio and metadata representations centered around an acoustic prior. Ex periments on BSD10K, BSD35K, and FSD50K show consistent improvements in both hierarchical single-label and multi-label classification. Compared with matched random-view scalar-fusion base lines, FAM-Gate improves the hierarchical F-score by 2.53 and 5.72 percentage points on BSD10K and BSD35K, respectively, while increasing macro mAP and macro F1 by 5.07 and 10.25 percentage points on FSD50K.

Computation and Language.title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
Computation and Language.summary: Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly little chemistry beyond what classical molecular features already capture.

Computation and Language.title: What Does a Discrete Diffusion Model Learn? One Reverse Process in Three Coordinates
Computation and Language.summary: What does a discrete diffusion model actually learn? The literature trains denoisers, bridge plug-ins, and concrete scores, each deriving its own ELBO objective under different conventions. This fragmentation makes the object being learned unclear and ELBO values difficult to interpret and compare. All three methods learn the same object in different coordinates: the exact time-reversal of the noising process. We first prove the Oracle Distance identity: for any noising process, the negative ELBO is not just a bound on the likelihood; it equals the data entropy plus the path KL divergence from the reversed noising process to the learned one. Next, for token-factorizing noise, we show that denoiser, bridge plug-in, and concrete score are three coordinates of this reverse process, derive exact conversions between them, and identify the probability distribution learned by each. In particular, contrary to its standard interpretation, the bridge plug-in learns not a denoiser but the cavity distribution: the clean token given the noisy sequence excluding its own position. We confirm the theory by training all three coordinates with masked, uniform, and GIDD kernels on OpenWebText under a shared recipe, and by training uniform-diffusion solvers on four logic tasks. The learned coordinates agree after conversion, while confusing the cavity with the denoiser can severely degrade sampling quality. Together with exact boundary-term formulas, closed-form NELBO calibrations at initialization, and a clock interpretation of time schedules, these results provide a conceptual framework and a mechanical recipe for deriving, implementing, and comparing discrete diffusion processes.
Computation and Language.comment: 48 pages, 10 figures. v2: revised and extended; accepted as an oral at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Diffusion Language Models: Foundations, Efficiency, and Reasoning

Computation and Language.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
Computation and Language.summary: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction

Computation and Language.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
Computation and Language.summary: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

Computation and Language.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
Computation and Language.summary: Brazilian Portuguese remains underserved by open-source language models, and the few that are safety-aligned rarely document what did not work or validate comparisons with statistical significance. We present Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, the second-generation post-training alignment of Manacá-1B (1.72B parameters, trained from scratch for PT-BR), with an SFT corpus of 291,223 examples. We document three DPO attempts, all negative, including a case where the training reward margin reaches 1.0 while free generation does not change at all, and show that safety came from a dedicated safety-SFT (LLM-jp AnswerCarefully style), refined over three iterations until closing the safety-helpfulness frontier. A controlled scan of the fraction of general data in the safety-SFT mix (10% to 60%) reveals a non-monotonic over-refusal curve with a knee point at 40-50%. The final model is compared against four external PT-BR models on the same items, with Wilson confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction: the lower bound of its safety interval (94.1%) lies above the upper bound of all four baselines. We also report a methodological finding for LLM-judge evaluation: on two of six safety items in MT-Bench-PT, the judge categorically refuses to assign a score regardless of the evaluated response, silently reducing the effective N of that category in every prior report of the project. We complement this with an n-gram decontamination check and a Chinchilla-anchored compute-budget table that attributes the gap in general capability to pre-training scale rather than alignment methodology. All code, raw data, logs, and scripts that produce every reported number are publicly released.

Computation and Language.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
Computation and Language.summary:
Automated research with LLM agents has shown promising results in various domains. Through iterative refinement and scored verifiers, LLM agents are capable of discovering new ideas. There are different ways to scale automated research: let one agent iterate for longer, run several agents in parallel, or further let the parallel agents communicate and build on one another's candidates. However, we find that all three strategies eventually plateau as the agents accumulate history. Each agent becomes anchored to its own past attempts, making fewer and smaller edits. Beyond this point, additional budget brings little further improvement. In this paper, we show that the key to scaling discovery further is to forget. Periodically discarding the search state, including every agent's session and the candidate history, and restarting from the best candidate found so far, unblocks the search and pushes the same budget further.
  We implement forgetting in a team of agents with communication and evaluate it on four tasks spanning heuristic programming, kernel optimization and model training. The results show up to 15% improvement compared to parallel agents, and up to 39% compared to a single agent. Our results suggest that, for open-ended discovery, what an agent is allowed to remember matters as much as how much compute it is given.

Computation and Language.title: Old Ideas, Novel Problems: The Instability of LLM-Based Novelty Evaluation
Computation and Language.summary: AI-based ideation systems are often evaluated on the novelty of their ideas, and that judgment is increasingly delegated to large language models. Such judges are typically built ad hoc and validated, if at all, on human-authored papers rather than on the generated ideas they are meant to score. So, how do novelty judges perform? Not well. We present a systematic controlled study of novelty evaluation design choices. We build an evaluation set automatically, mining OpenReview for passages where reviewers explicitly affirm or dispute a paper's originality and keeping only submissions with unanimous agreement at the extremes of their research area; we pair these with ideas from a vanilla LLM generator. Across six judges, we find that seemingly small prompt design choices have large consequences; e.g., simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs it is shown, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points and occasionally pushing it below chance. The same change helps one judge and hurts another. Retrieval and larger reasoning budgets help little, and two purpose-built novelty evaluators are outperformed by our cheapest prompted baseline. These results raise questions about reported novelty gains of automated ideation systems, and call for robust novelty evaluation methods.

Computation and Language.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
Computation and Language.summary: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.
Computation and Language.comment: 25 pages, 17 figures, 10 tables. Ali Zamani and Soroush Esfahanian contributed equally

Computation and Language.title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
Computation and Language.summary: Multimodal code intelligence connects the symbolic world of programs with the visual world their execution creates. Interest in this capability is burgeoning, as models are increasingly asked to produce charts, webpages, animations, and semi-structured documents. Recently, proprietary models have pushed far ahead, producing interactive artifacts even from a text description or a screenshot alone. Yet their data and training remain closed, and open progress is held back by the quantity and quality of available data and by the pipelines and methods for producing it. Quality is the harder of the two, since a sample must be correct as a program, well built, and above all visually right once rendered. No existing signal covers all three. Execution often returns just a pass or fail, code similarity does not map to the visual output, and task-specific verifiers do not generalize. To push open progress further, we start from the data side with PrismaForge, a hierarchical data pipeline centered on a synthesized rubric that decomposes these factors into checkable criteria. The same rubric serves as both filter and reward: it curates the supervised corpus, then drives reinforcement learning on visual-coding tasks. Leveraging PrismaForge for data synthesis and filtering, we build PrismaCoder-2M, the most diverse open dataset for multimodal code intelligence and the largest to date. On the model side, we train PrismaCoder-9B and PrismaCoder-35B on this data and release both. They lead the open state of the art by a wide margin and rival leading proprietary systems. Our analyses further show that the proposed rubric-based pipeline improves multimodal coding performance across model backbones. We release our code and data at https://qiushisun.github.io/PrismaCoder-Home/.

Computation and Language.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
Computation and Language.summary: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves. Our code is available at https://github.com/cii030/VASPO.

Computation and Language.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
Computation and Language.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

Computation and Language.title: From Clicks to Intent: Cross-Platform Session Embeddings with LLM-Distilled Taxonomy for Financial Services Recommendations
Computation and Language.summary: Sequential user behavior modeling is widely adopted in industrial recommender systems; however, significant gaps remain in financial services, where pre-login web interactions and authenticated in-app experiences differ drastically. Specifically, pre-login web users typically explore new products, whereas logged-in app users focus on account servicing. Due to the challenge of cross-channel entity resolution (e.g., matching anonymous web sessions to authenticated mobile accounts), web-based intent signals remain underutilized for post-authentication personalization.
